methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective multicenter cohort of 135 patients (119 de novo FL, 16 tFL) with FFPE-derived DNA, Oncomine 409-gene panel (1.65 Mb), standardized variant calling with documented filters (VAF ≥5%, ≥60 reads, homopolymer exclusion, cytosine deamination score ≤1), and thoughtful additional 64-gene panel for pathway analyses. Strengths include paired diagnosis-relapse samples (n=25), multivariate Cox models with C-index/CPE/BIC/AIC, and maximally selected rank statistics to determine the TMB threshold. Appropriate non-parametric comparisons (Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn/Bonferroni) and Wilcoxon signed-rank for paired analyses. Limitations: discrete TMB contributions (~0.8 mut/Mb per variant) near the cutoff (2.55 mut/Mb) are acknowledged but could be sensitive to noise; data-derived threshold may be optimistic without external validation; FFPE-based sequencing may introduce artifacts despite mitigations; tFL cohort too small for independent survival analysis.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective individual prognostic cohort study maps to Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is significant: POD24 identification is a major unmet need in FL, and TMB adds independent prognostic information to FLIPI with improved model metrics. TMB was also associated with fewer mTORC1 alterations and actionable EZH2 dynamics at relapse, directly relevant to tazemetostat use. Requires prospective validation before clinical adoption.

reporting_quality.justification: Biomarker/prognostic study where REMARK is the most applicable standard. Patient selection, treatment, follow-up definitions (PFS, LSS, OS), variant interpretation (ACMG/AMP, AMP/CAP guidelines), and statistical handling of multivariate models are described in detail. The maximally selected rank statistic for cutoff selection is appropriately disclosed as data-driven. Limitations are explicitly stated. Data availability is limited—no repository deposit is mentioned for the sequencing data and no analysis code is shared, hence data availability score of 2. REMARK checklist not explicitly provided.

novelty_literature.justification: TMB prognostication in FL has been sparsely studied (Tsukamoto et al. ref 35 used WES, Russler-Germain Alliance A151303 ref 44). This study's contributions: one of the largest dedicated FL TMB cohorts using a clinically pragmatic targeted panel; identification of TMB-t(14;18), BCL2, TNFRSF14, GNA13/GNAI2 associations; enrichment of mTORC1 alterations in low-TMB group; paired diagnosis-relapse TMB stability analysis showing clonal dynamics without overall TMB change; extension to tFL. These collectively represent a meaningful novel contribution to FL prognostics.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear methods, structured results, and a carefully calibrated discussion that places findings in context of discordant DLBCL literature and Alliance A151303. Numbers are reported precisely with CIs, p-values, and HR metrics. Figures/Tables are referenced consistently. The pathway categorization and clonal evolution analyses are clearly explained. Minor points: occasional dense technical passages and some redundancy between results and discussion.

key_strengths: Large dedicated FL TMB cohort (n=119 de novo + 16 tFL) with long follow-up and multivariate modeling showing TMB adds independent prognostic value beyond FLIPI (improved C-index, CPE, BIC, AIC)
Biologically coherent findings linking high TMB to t(14;18), BCL2/TNFRSF14 mutations, and GNA13/GNAI2 migration-pathway alterations; low TMB enriched for mTORC1-pathway mutations
Paired diagnosis-relapse analysis (n=25) revealing clonal dynamics (POD24 patients often retain all diagnostic variants) and actionable EZH2 gain/loss at relapse
Appropriate biomarker statistical methods including maximally selected rank statistics for cutoff and model-performance metrics; transparent about panel-based TMB limitations
Application of ACMG/AMP and AMP/CAP variant classification guidelines for pathway analyses
key_concerns: Data-derived optimal TMB cutoff (2.55 mut/Mb) is not validated in an independent external cohort, raising risk of overfitting
Near-cutoff sensitivity: each variant contributes approximately 0.8 mut/Mb so TMB classification may be brittle for samples close to threshold
tFL cohort (n=16) is too small for independent survival analysis; interpretation remains exploratory
No REMARK checklist explicitly provided; no deposition of sequencing data in a public repository; no analysis code
The relapse clonal-evolution analysis is based on 25 paired samples with heterogeneous treatment histories, limiting generalizability
One citation has a redacted URL (ref 26) that should be resolved before final publication
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically solid, clinically meaningful prognostic biomarker study addressing an unmet need in FL risk stratification; plausibly reaches Tier 2 specialty journals after major revisions to add external validation of the TMB cutoff and deposit sequencing data, otherwise firmly Tier 3 minor revisions.
